Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Our plan is to secure a better future for you and your family at every stage of life by sticking to a clear Conservative approach: a strong economy first; rewarding hard work; backing aspiration; protecting the vulnerable; and keeping our country safe.

Economy and tax
- Finish the job: eliminate the deficit, run a surplus and start paying down debt to keep taxes and mortgage rates low.
- No rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; new Tax‑Free Minimum Wage law.
- Crack down on tax evasion and aggressive avoidance; keep competitive business taxes and cut £10bn more red tape.
- Rebalance growth: build the Northern Powerhouse, devolve powers and business rates growth, and back elected metro mayors.
- Invest over £100bn in infrastructure: HS2/HS3, road upgrades, frozen commuter fares, universal broadband, better mobile and 5G.

Jobs, skills and business
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment with tougher Day One requirements and a time‑limited Youth Allowance.
- Support SMEs with a business rates review, Start Up Loans, prompt payment and a permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Invest in science, innovation and high‑value industries; boost the rural economy and champion British farming and fishing.

Fair welfare and family support
- Make work pay: lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; roll out Universal Credit; freeze working‑age benefits (with key exemptions).
- 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare; back marriage with transferable allowances.

Controlled immigration
- Keep net migration to the tens of thousands by reforming EU welfare rules, enforcing exit checks, clamping down on illegal working and exploitation, introducing a Controlling Migration Fund, and requiring fluent English in public‑facing roles.

Education and opportunity
- Protect per‑pupil funding; zero tolerance of failure; tougher standards in literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs.
- Turn every failing/coasting school into an academy; open 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and Degree Apprenticeships.
- Lift the cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; maintain world‑class research.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver a truly 7‑day NHS, same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s, named GPs, and digital access.
- Lead on cancer, mental health parity, dementia research; integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs.

Homes and ownership
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and introduce Help to Buy ISAs; build 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for under‑40s.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; prioritise brownfield; protect the Green Belt.

Law, security and justice
- Finish police reform; strengthen victims’ rights with a Victims’ Law; tackle extremism with new powers; reform prisons to cut reoffending.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down through competition, smart meters and efficiency; back new nuclear, gas and promising renewables; halt new subsidies for onshore wind; support least‑cost carbon cuts.
- Protect nature with a UK and Overseas Territories Blue Belt; strengthen flood defences; plant 11 million more trees.

Culture, society and the Union
- Free entry to national museums; freeze the BBC licence fee; back creative industries and school sport; expand National Citizen Service and offer three days’ paid volunteering.
- Protect pensioners: triple lock, single‑tier pension, pension freedoms, retain key benefits; raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m.
- Strengthen the Union: English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; support a stable, prosperous Northern Ireland.

Europe and the world
- Renegotiate Britain’s EU relationship and hold an in‑out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; reclaim powers; complete major trade deals.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces, renew Trident, meet NATO commitments; uphold 0.7% aid to tackle poverty, conflict and disease.

This is a disciplined, long‑term Conservative plan to reward work, back aspiration, protect vital services, and keep Britain strong, secure and free.

TEXT_G:
Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone

The Liberal Democrats set out a five‑year plan for an open, optimistic, outward‑looking UK that combines sound finances with social justice, green growth and equal rights.

Responsible finances and fair taxes
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18 with a fair mix of savings and taxes on wealth, big banks and polluters; debt to fall year on year thereafter.
- No rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax; raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; clamp down on avoidance and non‑dom status; levy on high‑value property.

Prosperity for all: a high‑skill, low‑carbon economy
- Long‑term Industrial Strategy; double economy‑wide R&D; expand apprenticeships and National Colleges; devolve economic levers locally.
- Reform finance: stronger British Business Bank; more competition, community and alternative finance.
- Green leadership: Zero Carbon Britain by 2050; expand the Green Investment Bank; end unabated coal by 2025; set a 2030 power decarbonisation target with up to 60% renewables; back community energy; tight fracking rules with revenues funding the transition.
- Modern infrastructure: HS2 as part of a UK‑wide network, rail electrification, city‑region transport, clean air zones, ultra‑low‑emission vehicle rollout, near‑universal high‑speed broadband.
- Open, trading nation: stay in a reformed EU, complete the Single Market, support fair trade deals, welcome talent and students.

Real help for families and work
- Expand free childcare to 20 hours for ages 2–4 and from nine months for working parents, complete Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Make work pay through Universal Credit; protect disability benefits; promote flexible work and Shared Parental Leave; transparency to close the gender pay gap; Living Wage in central government.
- Pensions: make the Triple Lock permanent; continue auto‑enrolment; fairer, simpler savings.

World‑class education, cradle to college
- Protect funding from nursery to 19; strengthen the Pupil Premium; qualified teachers in every class.
- End child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025; a slim core curriculum including PSHE, financial literacy and age‑appropriate SRE; independent standards body.
- Double firms hiring apprentices; improve FE; widen university access and protect income‑contingent finance; discount bus travel for 16–21s.

Health, care and wellbeing
- Invest at least £8bn extra a year in England’s NHS by 2020; integrate health and social care; improve GP access.
- Parity for mental health with waiting‑time standards and a £500m uplift; better children’s and perinatal services; crisis care that ends use of police cells.
- Support carers with a £250 annual bonus and new rights; cap care costs; raise care quality.
- Public health first: curb junk food marketing to children, tobacco levy, proportionate e‑cig rules, minimum alcohol pricing, cleaner air and warmer homes.

Homes and greener places
- Build 300,000 homes a year with Garden Cities, public‑land development and a Housing Investment Bank.
- Boost affordable housing; “Rent to Own” and Help to Rent; stronger tenant protections.
- Green Buildings Act: upgrade homes to EPC Band C (fuel‑poor by 2027); council tax discount for major efficiency improvements.
- Five Green Laws: Nature, Zero Carbon, Green Transport, Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste, and Green Buildings; expand accessible green space and protect wildlife; support sustainable farming and fair food chains.

Freedom, justice and secure communities
- Protect the Human Rights Act; pass a Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; evidence‑led policing with local Police Boards; a Victims’ Bill of Rights.
- Tackle violence against women and girls; rehabilitate offenders with smart non‑custodial sentences; health‑led drug policy.
- Restore full entry/exit checks; fair, efficient asylum; welcome skilled migrants and students.

Power to people and nations
- Home Rule within a federal UK; a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for Commons and local government; reformed Lords; cap big money in politics; devolution on demand in England.

Britain in the world
- Lead in the EU, NATO, UN and Commonwealth; support a safe, reformed EU; climate leadership (EU −50% by 2030; zero‑carbon UK by 2050); step down nuclear posture while maintaining security; keep aid at 0.7%; champion human rights and LGBT+ equality worldwide.
